evidence.excerpt:
Targeted treatments include small molecules and therapeutic antibodies with different actions. A molecule whose function supports cancer growth and a surface molecule used to deliver an active drug or recruit an immune cell have different roles. Detecting either does not by itself establish that the finished treatment reaches its target, changes a relevant function or helps in a particular clinical setting.

Some treatments require a specified biomarker test; others have no target-expression selection test in the relevant label. Keep the actual drug, disease, treatment setting and testing rule together. NCI describes resistance and potentially serious adverse effects of targeted therapy. Neither relative normal-tissue sparing, mild toxicity nor a permanent response follows from the word targeted.

A drug target is a biological molecule or structure that a treatment acts on, and the mechanism of action explains how that action produces an effect. The National Cancer Institute describes targeted therapy as treatment that targets proteins that control how cancer cells grow, divide and spread, and says most targeted therapies are small-molecule drugs, which are small enough to enter cells and so suit targets inside cells, or monoclonal antibodies, which are designed to attach to specific targets on cancer cells. It describes antibodies that mark cancer cells for the immune system, antibodies that stop growth or cause self-destruction directly, and antibodies that carry toxins to cancer cells. These are different jobs, so a shared label of targeted does not make the mechanisms interchangeable, and a target that is only an address for delivery need not drive the cancer's growth.

An altered gene or an elevated protein can suggest a target hypothesis; it does not show that inhibiting the target will harm cancer cells selectively, which controlled perturbations of the target test, and safe exposure and appropriate clinical studies answer later questions. Naming a target answers only the first of several questions. Binding is an interaction between molecules and can be shown with a purified protein, which does not show that the compound reaches the protein inside a cell. Target engagement asks whether the interaction occurs in the relevant cells or tissue, and exposure, target location and the cell membrane all bear on it; a blood concentration and a concentration at an intracellular target are different observations. The cellular thermal shift assay of Martinez Molina and colleagues was developed to evaluate drug binding to target proteins in cells and tissue samples, and its authors used it to monitor drug transport and activation, off-target effects and resistance in cancer cell lines. Binding is also different from changing function: a compound can inhibit an enzyme, activate a receptor or deliver a payload, and a binder can leave the target's activity unchanged. Binding assays test an interaction under specified conditions and engagement assays examine the relevant cells or tissue, while a downstream signal measures a biological consequence and is not automatically a direct measure of how much of the target is occupied; growth, death and regrowth assays add further layers. A measured change in signalling, division or survival needs controls that test the proposed explanation, and one positive experiment should not carry the whole claim.

The last step is clinical. Mechanistic plausibility does not show benefit, because the target may also be present in healthy tissue and the useful margin depends on achieved benefit and harm in a stated disease, treatment setting, product and outcome. The National Cancer Institute adds that cancer cells can become resistant to targeted therapy when the target itself changes so the drug can no longer interact with it, or when cells find new ways to grow that do not depend on the target.

Worked example, fictional. An antibody binds protein A on cancer cells, and a growth assay shows no change. Binding is supported under the assay conditions. It has not been shown that protein A drives growth, that the antibody inhibits protein A's function, that a finished payload-bearing product delivers anything, or that the product is safe and beneficial; each of those needs its own evidence. Before saying a drug worked, name the layer that was measured.

Follow the complete construct through separate measurements. Controlled binding to viable cells tests an accessible recognition feature; fixed-tissue staining alone does not. A trafficking assay must distinguish surface-bound from internal material. Measuring the relevant released payload or catabolite at its site of action tests a later step, and a payload-appropriate functional readout and survival over time answer further questions. A fluorescent antibody-associated tag can remain detectable without demonstrating that active drug reached that compartment. Keep assay sensitivity, time, concentration, cellular denominator and controls with each result; no one of these measurements establishes delivery throughout a tumour or clinical benefit.

evidence.excerpt:
A conventional alpha-beta T-cell receptor uses paired chains to recognise a peptide-HLA surface. Its recognition chains assemble with CD3 signalling partners, as demonstrated in the human TCR-CD3 structural study. CDR3 is an informative variable region, but neither a beta-chain sequence nor CDR3 alone specifies the complete paired receptor or its function.

Particular receptors can cross-react across peptide and HLA contexts; that does not establish a universal cross-reactivity rate. Paired receptor identity, binding, activation, target-cell death and clinical benefit require different evidence. A response by one reconstructed pair to peptide-loaded cells does not establish that another alpha-chain pairing recognises the same target, or that either kills naturally presenting tumour cells. Use irrelevant-target, HLA and target-only viability controls. Peptide loading can bypass natural processing, and contact diagrams are not healthy-tissue safety tests.

CAR-T cell therapy uses T cells carrying a chimeric antigen receptor to recognize a target. FDA-approved products include CD19- and BCMA-directed CAR-T cells for selected blood cancers, including B-cell leukemias, lymphomas and multiple myeloma. The individual product label defines the treatment setting and eligibility. A common autologous approach collects a person’s T cells, engineers and expands them outside the body, then infuses them back; conditioning and follow-up depend on the protocol.

A common antibody-derived CAR joins an external binding region, a hinge or spacer, a membrane anchor and intracellular signaling domains. The receptor is a protein; its encoding instructions and the living cell carrying it are different objects. Approved products and experimental constructs differ in cell source, receptor, manufacturing and clinical setting. Product labels and trial records define their actual uses; a platform name does not establish eligibility or benefit.

In early work, Gross, Waks and Eshhar joined antibody-variable regions to T-cell receptor components in 1989. Eshhar and colleagues subsequently tested single-chain antibody-binding regions joined to gamma or zeta signaling chains in 1993. These experimental designs helped separate recognition from the signaling machinery attached to it.

FDA-approved examples include tisagenlecleucel, axicabtagene ciloleucel, lisocabtagene maraleucel, brexucabtagene autoleucel, obecabtagene autoleucel, idecabtagene vicleucel and ciltacabtagene autoleucel. Their labeled diseases, treatment settings and eligibility differ; the individual product records retain those distinctions.

A dosed T-cell engager supplies a protein connecting target recognition to an available T cell. It does not itself install receptor instructions or supply engineered living responders. Product design can use antibody-derived binding fragments or a soluble TCR recognition domain; some target arms require a particular peptide-HLA complex. Compact BiTE designs, Fc-containing architectures and half-life extension describe features that can overlap rather than mutually exclusive treatment categories.

Clinical examples include blinatumomab in B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia, teclistamab in multiple myeloma and tarlatamab in extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer. Their actual labels define different settings, combinations, prior treatments and harms. Tebentafusp is a peptide-HLA-directed soluble TCR/CD3 protein with its own allele- and disease-specific use. Neither a common platform name nor binding in a laboratory establishes eligibility or comparative benefit.

Trastuzumab can inhibit proliferation and recruit antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity; the related HER2 antibody in trastuzumab deruxtecan carries a TOP1-inhibitor payload. An ADC and a surface T-cell engager differ in processing versus productive contact with useful effectors. An engager recruits responders, whereas a CAR-T product supplies engineered living cells with their own survival, expansion and trafficking. A radioligand's carrier distribution and radiation deposition differ from chemical-payload delivery. Sharing an address does not equalise any of these actions, exposure histories or normal-tissue risks. With a clinical claim, record disease, biomarker definition, prior care, comparator, endpoint, follow-up and harms alongside the actual product; access or eligibility cannot supply an unmeasured efficacy comparison.

A change of format is a new product hypothesis. If an ADC binds M but yields little active material after uptake, an M-directed engager might avoid that particular processing requirement. It still needs its own binding and contact-geometry measurements, useful effector access and function, normal-tissue testing and clinical evidence. Earlier antibody or ADC tolerability does not establish the safety of a different action. Bystander delivery and two-address designs are possible responses to heterogeneous expression, not guaranteed coverage or an exhaustive list of solutions.

On-target, off-tumour toxicity is injury from recognition of the intended target on healthy tissue. It differs from recognition of an unintended molecular target. The predictable, lymphoma-specific consequences of aiming at lineage antigens (B-cell aplasia, low immunoglobulin, and the effects of CD52, CCR4 and CD47 targeting) are described in the record on the cost of aiming at a lineage antigen, which this record does not repeat.

Many candidate cancer targets are normal proteins found at different levels or places in the body, so tumour-associated does not mean tumour-exclusive. A treatment that recognises its intended target wherever it is accessible, such as a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell, can harm any healthy tissue that displays it, and tissue location, target density, receptor properties and exposure all shape the outcome. This differs from off-target cross-reactivity, in which the receptor recognises an unintended molecule, and from cytokine release syndrome, which is systemic inflammatory activation; the three can occur together. It also differs from payload toxicity in an antibody-drug conjugate: a pooled analysis of ADC trials found the key grade 3 to 4 toxicities grouped by payload and concluded they were likely off-target and related to the payload (Masters et al., 2018). Binding specificity is not tissue selectivity, and experience with an antibody against a target does not automatically carry over to a living cell with a different recognition and signalling system.

Two primary reports show the contrast. A patient with colon cancer metastatic to the lungs and liver received 10 billion autologous T cells expressing a trastuzumab-based CAR against ERBB2 (HER2), the largest number permitted in the first dose-escalation cohort, the day after a lymphodepleting regimen of cyclophosphamide (60 mg/kg daily for 2 days) and fludarabine (25 mg/m2 for 5 days). Within 15 minutes the patient had respiratory distress, chest imaging showed pulmonary oedema, and the patient died 5 days after treatment, with marked rises in interferon-gamma, GM-CSF, tumour necrosis factor-alpha, interleukin-6 and interleukin-10. At autopsy multiple organs showed systemic ischaemia and haemorrhagic microangiopathic injury and the lungs diffuse alveolar damage; histological examination of autopsy tissue found ERBB2 at 3+ in liver metastases and 2+ in lung metastases and much lower levels in normal lung parenchyma, normal liver and normal breast. The authors hypothesised that highly active ERBB2-directed T cells recognised ERBB2 on normal lung cells on first pass through the lung and released inflammatory cytokines that began a cascade ending in multiorgan failure; the autopsy findings were read as initial lung injury followed by days of hypotension and ischaemia, and the authors call the significance of the cells' reactivity against cultured primary cells unclear. This is a single case, with a stated dose and conditioning, whose mechanism is the authors' hypothesis and which gives no incidence for any CAR product (Morgan et al., 2010). In a trial of an affinity-enhanced T-cell receptor against HLA-A*01-restricted MAGE-A3 in myeloma and melanoma, the first two patients developed cardiogenic shock and died within days; no MAGE-A3 expression was detected in heart tissue at autopsy, and beating cardiomyocytes made from induced pluripotent stem cells triggered T-cell killing through recognition of an unrelated peptide from titin. That is off-target recognition of an unintended molecule, not the intended target in the wrong tissue (Linette et al., 2013).

How the question is asked before and during trials. FDA's CAR T-cell development guidance says to assess both undesired targeting of healthy tissue that expresses the intended antigen (on-target/off-tumour) and unintended targeting of other antigens, using examples such as tissue cross-reactivity studies with an antibody carrying the same recognition domain, protein arrays, cytotoxicity and cytokine-release testing on panels of primary cells, cell lines or stem-cell-derived organ systems, and relevant animal models, and encourages a combination of methods; antigen recognition domains can differ in affinity or avidity or recognise a different site, which should be evaluated, and CAR T cells can carry added components such as suicide genes. In practice a readout is a staining intensity or positive fraction, a binding profile, killing or cytokine release by healthy cells at a named time, and finally organ injury in the treated population; stained fixed tissue does not show a living organ's accessibility, an animal model may lack the human target, and a negative result in one panel is not a safety certificate. No universal expression cut-off is given here because no source read gives one. Whether affinity tuning, recognition logic or control switches improve safety for a particular design needs that design's own evidence. The 2026 ASTCT consensus abstract lists on-target, off-tumour toxicity among the toxicities for which it considered definitions and grading; its criteria were not readable.

A prespecified exploratory biomarker analysis had TROP2 data for 290 of the 468 primary-population patients. The authors supported benefit in the high and medium groups and considered the low group too small for a definitive conclusion. The absence of a TROP2 label-selection requirement is a separate regulatory fact. Post hoc demographic and brain-metastasis analyses retain their own populations and uncertainty; none is a prospective validation of a universal marker cutoff.

DESTINY-Breast04 (NCT03734029) randomised 557 patients with HER2-low metastatic breast cancer after one or two prior lines of chemotherapy: 494 were hormone receptor-positive and 63 hormone receptor-negative at randomisation. HER2-low meant IHC 1+ or IHC 2+/ISH-negative. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival in the hormone receptor-positive cohort; key secondary endpoints included overall-population progression-free survival and overall survival. The 2022 report showed longer progression-free and overall survival with trastuzumab deruxtecan.

The study did not randomize IHC 0 tumours and does not establish a universal HER2-expression floor, biological category or eligibility for everyone with HER2-negative disease. Exploratory hormone receptor-negative analyses use their specified efficacy populations, distinct from the randomised stratification count. The later Nature Medicine report and current drug label are separate dated sources, not interchangeable versions of the original result.

FDA reports median PFS 10.8 versus 5.6 months (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.47 to 0.69) and OS 23.7 versus 18.7 months (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.64 to 0.98). FDA approved the advanced-disease indication May 22, 2026. evidence.excerpt:
A typical immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibody has two heavy and two light chains held together by molecular interactions and disulfide bonds. At each arm tip, variable regions from a heavy and a light chain together form a binding site; its sequence and three-dimensional shape influence what it recognises. Fab (fragment antigen-binding) names an arm containing the binding site and its associated constant domains, so it is not simply another word for the variable region. Fc (fragment crystallizable, a name that comes from an experimental property) names the remaining stem, built from CH2 and CH3 domains of both heavy chains in the familiar IgG description. Hinge flexibility changes how the arms are arranged. A drawn Y is a simplification: some natural and engineered formats omit familiar parts.

Fc can interact with immune-cell receptors and with complement, but compatible effectors, target arrangement and other conditions decide whether killing, engulfment or complement damage follows, so Fc is not an automatic kill command. Binding and effector contributions are separate and the finished molecule needs testing. Nimmerjahn and Ravetch (2005) showed in mouse experiments that IgG subclasses differ in the ratio of their binding to activating and inhibitory Fc receptors, which predicted in vivo activity; that is not a universal ranking of human antibody performance. An isotype is a heavy-chain class (see the isotypes and Fc silencing record). Structure alone does not identify the producing cell or establish what the antibody recognises.

The epitope is the molecular feature recognised and can be a folded protein surface or another accessible feature, not necessarily a short fragment displayed by HLA. Binding is measured against a defined antigen preparation and antibody concentration, sometimes in nanomoles per litre, and it matters whether the test used purified protein or intact cells, because folding, accessibility and multiple binding sites change the result. A concentration or fluorescence signal alone is not an affinity. Fc-receptor and complement interactions are tested separately from target binding, and neither binding nor a laboratory effector result establishes clinical benefit or safety. A blocking antibody, an antibody-drug conjugate and a bispecific format can share a target and still act differently.

A conventional alpha-beta T-cell receptor uses paired chains to recognise a peptide-HLA surface. Its recognition chains assemble with CD3 signalling partners, as demonstrated in the human TCR-CD3 structural study. CDR3 is an informative variable region, but neither a beta-chain sequence nor CDR3 alone specifies the complete paired receptor or its function.

Particular receptors can cross-react across peptide and HLA contexts; that does not establish a universal cross-reactivity rate. Paired receptor identity, binding, activation, target-cell death and clinical benefit require different evidence. A response by one reconstructed pair to peptide-loaded cells does not establish that another alpha-chain pairing recognises the same target, or that either kills naturally presenting tumour cells. Use irrelevant-target, HLA and target-only viability controls. Peptide loading can bypass natural processing, and contact diagrams are not healthy-tissue safety tests.

An antibody-derived TCR mimic recognizes a peptide-HLA complex using an antibody scaffold. A soluble TCR/CD3 engager instead uses a TCR-derived recognition scaffold attached to a recruiting arm. TCR-T administers cells carrying receptor chains. Target recognition, molecular scaffold and administered object are separate axes; a mimic can be part of an engager without becoming a TCR protein.

evidence.excerpt:
CAR-T cell therapy uses T cells carrying a chimeric antigen receptor to recognize a target. FDA-approved products include CD19- and BCMA-directed CAR-T cells for selected blood cancers, including B-cell leukemias, lymphomas and multiple myeloma. The individual product label defines the treatment setting and eligibility. A common autologous approach collects a person’s T cells, engineers and expands them outside the body, then infuses them back; conditioning and follow-up depend on the protocol.

A common antibody-derived CAR joins an external binding region, a hinge or spacer, a membrane anchor and intracellular signaling domains. The receptor is a protein; its encoding instructions and the living cell carrying it are different objects. Approved products and experimental constructs differ in cell source, receptor, manufacturing and clinical setting. Product labels and trial records define their actual uses; a platform name does not establish eligibility or benefit.

In early work, Gross, Waks and Eshhar joined antibody-variable regions to T-cell receptor components in 1989. Eshhar and colleagues subsequently tested single-chain antibody-binding regions joined to gamma or zeta signaling chains in 1993. These experimental designs helped separate recognition from the signaling machinery attached to it.

FDA-approved examples include tisagenlecleucel, axicabtagene ciloleucel, lisocabtagene maraleucel, brexucabtagene autoleucel, obecabtagene autoleucel, idecabtagene vicleucel and ciltacabtagene autoleucel. Their labeled diseases, treatment settings and eligibility differ; the individual product records retain those distinctions.

A common CAR presents a binder outside the cell and signaling domains inside it, connected through a spacer and transmembrane region. Conventional surface-antigen recognition can bypass peptide-HLA presentation; specialized peptide-HLA-targeting CARs retain the relevant HLA and antigen-processing requirements.

Liddy studied soluble TCR/CD3 ImmTAC proteins in experimental systems. Dao studied an antibody-derived WT1/HLA-A*02:01/CD3 engager in cells and mice. Their results do not establish clinical benefit for every scaffold, HLA allele or cancer. Recruiting another T cell does not require that cell’s native receptor to recognize the target, but does not remove the target arm’s HLA restriction.

evidence.excerpt:
Pharmacokinetics describes absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion. A dose is an administered amount; exposure describes a named substance's concentration over time in a specified compartment. Route, organ function, metabolism, binding and interactions can make equal doses produce different exposure.

The December 2016 FDA labelling guidance asks for measures such as maximum plasma concentration, concentration-time area under the curve, clearance, accumulation and half-life in their relevant conditions. These measurements inform dosage selection alongside activity, safety and tolerability; they do not establish benefit on their own. For conjugated drugs, active metabolites and radiopharmaceuticals, specify which component was measured. Blood concentration is not automatically the concentration of active material at a cancer-cell target.

Dose, exposure and effect are three different things. Dose is the administered amount; exposure is a named substance's concentration over time in a named place, which route, organ function, interactions and product properties can change for the same dose; and effect is a separate measurement, because effects or injury can persist after exposure falls and detectable drug does not guarantee productive engagement. Pharmacokinetics follows absorption (including how much of an oral dose reaches the circulation), distribution (plasma is not the unbound concentration inside a cell), metabolism (active metabolites may add their own exposure) and excretion, summarised by clearance, the removal relative to concentration, in volume per time. FDA labelling guidance lists the maximum plasma concentration (Cmax) and area under the concentration-time curve (AUC) at the approved dosage, time to steady state, accumulation ratio, clearance, volume of distribution and half-life; this AUC is an exposure area and is unrelated to the area under a prediction curve that judges tests.

evidence.excerpt:
A drug's half-life describes a halving of the concentration of a named substance in a specified phase or model. Early distribution, terminal elimination and the effective half-life relevant to accumulation can differ. With nonlinear elimination, a reported value can also depend on the dose. The December 2016 FDA clinical-pharmacology labelling guidance distinguishes effective from terminal half-life and asks for the conditions needed to interpret each.

Concentration and effect need separate measurements. Active metabolites, persistent biological changes and tissue injury can matter after the measured parent drug has declined. Living cell products can expand rather than simply disappear, and a radiopharmaceutical combines physical decay with biological removal. A half-life alone supplies no universal treatment schedule or recovery clock.

Compare requirements rather than rank formats. Trastuzumab can inhibit proliferation and recruit antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity; the related HER2 antibody in trastuzumab deruxtecan carries a TOP1-inhibitor payload. An ADC and a surface T-cell engager differ in processing versus productive contact with useful effectors. An engager recruits responders, whereas a CAR-T product supplies engineered living cells with their own survival, expansion and trafficking. A radioligand's carrier distribution and radiation deposition differ from chemical-payload delivery. Sharing an address does not equalise any of these actions, exposure histories or normal-tissue risks. evidence.excerpt: Radiation can deposit energy beyond the cell carrying the radioactive product, so chemical-payload uptake into each neighbouring cell is not the same requirement. Binding and internalisation can affect retention, but the complete carrier's distribution, biological removal, radionuclide decay and tissue geometry still determine delivery. A diagnostic tracer image is not a measured therapeutic absorbed dose, and resistance to a chemotherapy payload does not itself establish radiation sensitivity or safe organ exposure.

Sgouros's 2020 review labels its table values approximate emission range in tissue: 0.62 mm for lutetium-177 beta emission, and 0.05 to 0.08 mm for the listed radium-223, actinium-225 and thorium-227 alpha emitters. That column does not identify the values as mean or maximum ranges, so they should not silently be relabelled as either or used as exact treatment boundaries. The isotope and range convention matter; one beta or alpha number is not a value for every radionuclide. FDA's 2019 radiopharmaceutical guidance separately defines physical, biological and effective half-life and time-integrated activity.

Radioactive activity is a decay rate in becquerels; absorbed dose is deposited energy per mass in gray. A single bright image is not time-integrated exposure. Dosimetry combines suitable activity measurements or models over time with tissue geometry and emission properties. Neither the targeting-molecule mass nor the administered activity alone specifies tumor dose.

rows.entailment: Decay, biological distribution and dose differ; tracer brightness does not establish time-integrated therapeutic dose or organ safety.
rows.sourceScope: FDA 2019 glossary and Sgouros selected review table/body.

evidence.excerpt:
On-target, off-tumour toxicity is injury from recognition of the intended target on healthy tissue. It differs from recognition of an unintended molecular target. The predictable, lymphoma-specific consequences of aiming at lineage antigens (B-cell aplasia, low immunoglobulin, and the effects of CD52, CCR4 and CD47 targeting) are described in the record on the cost of aiming at a lineage antigen, which this record does not repeat.

Many candidate cancer targets are normal proteins found at different levels or places in the body, so tumour-associated does not mean tumour-exclusive. A treatment that recognises its intended target wherever it is accessible, such as a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell, can harm any healthy tissue that displays it, and tissue location, target density, receptor properties and exposure all shape the outcome. This differs from off-target cross-reactivity, in which the receptor recognises an unintended molecule, and from cytokine release syndrome, which is systemic inflammatory activation; the three can occur together. It also differs from payload toxicity in an antibody-drug conjugate: a pooled analysis of ADC trials found the key grade 3 to 4 toxicities grouped by payload and concluded they were likely off-target and related to the payload (Masters et al., 2018). Binding specificity is not tissue selectivity, and experience with an antibody against a target does not automatically carry over to a living cell with a different recognition and signalling system.

Two primary reports show the contrast. A patient with colon cancer metastatic to the lungs and liver received 10 billion autologous T cells expressing a trastuzumab-based CAR against ERBB2 (HER2), the largest number permitted in the first dose-escalation cohort, the day after a lymphodepleting regimen of cyclophosphamide (60 mg/kg daily for 2 days) and fludarabine (25 mg/m2 for 5 days). Within 15 minutes the patient had respiratory distress, chest imaging showed pulmonary oedema, and the patient died 5 days after treatment, with marked rises in interferon-gamma, GM-CSF, tumour necrosis factor-alpha, interleukin-6 and interleukin-10. At autopsy multiple organs showed systemic ischaemia and haemorrhagic microangiopathic injury and the lungs diffuse alveolar damage; histological examination of autopsy tissue found ERBB2 at 3+ in liver metastases and 2+ in lung metastases and much lower levels in normal lung parenchyma, normal liver and normal breast. The authors hypothesised that highly active ERBB2-directed T cells recognised ERBB2 on normal lung cells on first pass through the lung and released inflammatory cytokines that began a cascade ending in multiorgan failure; the autopsy findings were read as initial lung injury followed by days of hypotension and ischaemia, and the authors call the significance of the cells' reactivity against cultured primary cells unclear. This is a single case, with a stated dose and conditioning, whose mechanism is the authors' hypothesis and which gives no incidence for any CAR product (Morgan et al., 2010). In a trial of an affinity-enhanced T-cell receptor against HLA-A*01-restricted MAGE-A3 in myeloma and melanoma, the first two patients developed cardiogenic shock and died within days; no MAGE-A3 expression was detected in heart tissue at autopsy, and beating cardiomyocytes made from induced pluripotent stem cells triggered T-cell killing through recognition of an unrelated peptide from titin. That is off-target recognition of an unintended molecule, not the intended target in the wrong tissue (Linette et al., 2013).

How the question is asked before and during trials. FDA's CAR T-cell development guidance says to assess both undesired targeting of healthy tissue that expresses the intended antigen (on-target/off-tumour) and unintended targeting of other antigens, using examples such as tissue cross-reactivity studies with an antibody carrying the same recognition domain, protein arrays, cytotoxicity and cytokine-release testing on panels of primary cells, cell lines or stem-cell-derived organ systems, and relevant animal models, and encourages a combination of methods; antigen recognition domains can differ in affinity or avidity or recognise a different site, which should be evaluated, and CAR T cells can carry added components such as suicide genes. In practice a readout is a staining intensity or positive fraction, a binding profile, killing or cytokine release by healthy cells at a named time, and finally organ injury in the treated population; stained fixed tissue does not show a living organ's accessibility, an animal model may lack the human target, and a negative result in one panel is not a safety certificate. No universal expression cut-off is given here because no source read gives one. Whether affinity tuning, recognition logic or control switches improve safety for a particular design needs that design's own evidence. The 2026 ASTCT consensus abstract lists on-target, off-tumour toxicity among the toxicities for which it considered definitions and grading; its criteria were not readable.

M-Rabet's 2017 study found membranous Nectin-4 staining in 62% of 61 TNBCs and did not detect protein in the adult normal tissues examined by that assay. That negative assay result is not universal normal-tissue absence or a safety advantage. PADCEV, a different finished Nectin-4-directed construct, carries a boxed warning for severe and fatal skin reactions. Keep antibody, preparation, tissue coverage, detection limits, product and exposure with the comparison.

evidence.excerpt:
ASCENT (NCT02574455), published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2021, randomised 529 patients overall. The primary population comprised 468 without brain metastases. Sacituzumab govitecan improved progression-free and overall survival compared with physician’s-choice single-agent chemotherapy in that population. The randomised comparison does not establish equal effects at every TROP2 expression level.

A prespecified exploratory biomarker analysis had TROP2 data for 290 of the 468 primary-population patients. The authors supported benefit in the high and medium groups and considered the low group too small for a definitive conclusion. The absence of a TROP2 label-selection requirement is a separate regulatory fact. Post hoc demographic and brain-metastasis analyses retain their own populations and uncertainty; none is a prospective validation of a universal marker cutoff.

All 468 participants in the original primary population without brain metastases had previously received a taxane. The comparator was physician's-choice single-agent eribulin, vinorelbine, capecitabine or gemcitabine. The 2021 progression-free and overall-survival results belong to that previously treated metastatic population; they are not a comparison between two ADCs or evidence for postoperative use or use after a specified prior TOP1 conjugate.

Design (NEJM 2021): 529 patients with relapsed or refractory metastatic triple-negative disease after at least two prior therapies randomised 1 to 1 to sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg on days 1 and 8 of 21 or physician's choice of eribulin, vinorelbine, capecitabine or gemcitabine; 468 without brain metastases formed the primary population. Progression-free survival 5.6 versus 1.7 months (hazard ratio 0.41), overall survival 12.1 versus 6.7 months (0.48), response 35 versus 5 percent; grade 3 or higher neutropenia 51 versus 33 percent, diarrhoea 10 versus below 1 percent. Post hoc subgroups (npj Breast Cancer 2024) reported longer progression-free and overall survival in the examined older and Black participant groups; these were exploratory comparisons, not prospective marker-interaction tests. In the stable-brain-metastasis subgroup, progression-free survival was numerically longer but overall survival similar.

evidence.excerpt: Delivery, active-payload action and cellular response can organise questions about failure, but they are not independent or validated clinical cause categories. A tumour can combine altered recognition or processing, export, a changed payload target, and repair or tolerance of injury. Sampling one site, time or plasma assay can miss other cells and mechanisms. A new address may leave a payload vulnerability intact; another payload may leave a delivery problem intact. The next discriminating test must examine the proposed explanation rather than infer it from the treatment name.

Three fictional resistant models motivate different tests. If M is lost but the active payload still works with verified delivery to its action site, investigate another accessible address and the finished product's delivery. If M remains but the tested TOP1 material does not work while a microtubule-directed material does, investigate another action rather than predicting a probability of failure for every TOP1 ADC. If a pump inhibitor restores activity, test the specific export hypothesis with suitable controls: the inhibitor can have other effects. PADCEV's label identifies MMAE as a P-glycoprotein substrate, so a microtubule class name alone does not promise escape from export.

rows.entailment: Delivery, payload action and response organise overlapping hypotheses. Neither format change nor one sampled mechanism validates a clinical cause classifier or automatic rescue.

evidence.excerpt: Four U.S. breast-cancer label examples separate address from payload: sacituzumab govitecan pairs TROP2 with SN-38, datopotamab deruxtecan pairs TROP2 with DXd, trastuzumab deruxtecan pairs HER2 with DXd, and trastuzumab emtansine pairs HER2 with DM1. SN-38 and DXd inhibit TOP1; DM1 acts on microtubules. Their indication and testing requirements differ, including the HER2-positive uses of T-DM1 and specified lower-expression uses of T-DXd. Changing the address or payload changes a design feature, not a measured probability of response. These examples are not an exhaustive U.S. or worldwide approval inventory.

The June 2026 US label retains unresectable locally advanced or metastatic TNBC after at least two systemic therapies, at least one for metastatic disease, and HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer after endocrine-based therapy and at least two additional systemic therapies in the metastatic setting. On June 24, 2026, FDA approved first-line advanced TNBC monotherapy when PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor therapy is unsuitable, and combination with pembrolizumab or pembrolizumab/berahyaluronidase alfa when PD-L1 CPS is at least 10 by an FDA-authorized test. The urothelial indication was withdrawn November 22, 2024. These indications do not establish postoperative recurrence prevention. The label has boxed warnings for neutropenia and diarrhea; a TROP2 companion test is not required.

FDA approved datopotamab deruxtecan on January 17, 2025 for adults with unresectable or metastatic HR-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer after endocrine-based therapy and chemotherapy for advanced disease. The June 23, 2025 accelerated approval covers locally advanced or metastatic EGFR-mutated NSCLC after EGFR-directed therapy and platinum chemotherapy. On May 22, 2026 FDA approved unresectable or metastatic TNBC when PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor therapy is unsuitable; supporting TROPION-Breast02 studied previously untreated advanced disease. It reported median OS 23.7 versus 18.7 months, HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.64 to 0.98), in 644 randomized patients. The label does not require a TROP2 companion test or establish postoperative recurrence prevention. Stomatitis, ocular toxicity and interstitial lung disease require monitoring.

The U.S. KADCYLA label specifies HER2-positive metastatic breast-cancer use after trastuzumab and a taxane under stated prior-treatment or recurrence conditions. It also specifies adjuvant use for HER2-positive early breast cancer with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant taxane and trastuzumab-based treatment, with selection by an FDA-authorised test.

The antibody binds HER2; uptake and lysosomal degradation release DM1-containing cytotoxic catabolites that inhibit microtubule assembly. The label also reports inhibition of HER2 signalling and antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity in vitro. A noncleavable-linker description does not establish which construct feature caused a clinical difference from another product.

evidence.excerpt: A new strategy is a hypothesis about a specified failure. A different microtubule-directed payload tests another action; a redesigned TOP1 payload can change transport or potency while retaining vulnerabilities. A repair or checkpoint inhibitor proposes changing the response to damage and remains a chemical intervention. A transcription inhibitor needs drug- and model-specific evidence, including any claim about noncycling cells. An immune-stimulating conjugate needs evidence for useful immune activation, its harms and any durable effect after exposure ends. Alpha-emitter proposals still need carrier distribution, retention, radiation dose and response evidence. Two-address or biparatopic binding can change delivery, but neither uniquely exhausts delivery strategies nor guarantees productive uptake. These categories overlap; a diagram does not establish exclusive failure classes or rank how predictable their safety will be.

On-target, off-tumour toxicity is injury from recognition of the intended target on healthy tissue. It differs from recognition of an unintended molecular target. The predictable, lymphoma-specific consequences of aiming at lineage antigens (B-cell aplasia, low immunoglobulin, and the effects of CD52, CCR4 and CD47 targeting) are described in the record on the cost of aiming at a lineage antigen, which this record does not repeat.

Many candidate cancer targets are normal proteins found at different levels or places in the body, so tumour-associated does not mean tumour-exclusive. A treatment that recognises its intended target wherever it is accessible, such as a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell, can harm any healthy tissue that displays it, and tissue location, target density, receptor properties and exposure all shape the outcome. This differs from off-target cross-reactivity, in which the receptor recognises an unintended molecule, and from cytokine release syndrome, which is systemic inflammatory activation; the three can occur together. It also differs from payload toxicity in an antibody-drug conjugate: a pooled analysis of ADC trials found the key grade 3 to 4 toxicities grouped by payload and concluded they were likely off-target and related to the payload (Masters et al., 2018). Binding specificity is not tissue selectivity, and experience with an antibody against a target does not automatically carry over to a living cell with a different recognition and signalling system.

Two primary reports show the contrast. A patient with colon cancer metastatic to the lungs and liver received 10 billion autologous T cells expressing a trastuzumab-based CAR against ERBB2 (HER2), the largest number permitted in the first dose-escalation cohort, the day after a lymphodepleting regimen of cyclophosphamide (60 mg/kg daily for 2 days) and fludarabine (25 mg/m2 for 5 days). Within 15 minutes the patient had respiratory distress, chest imaging showed pulmonary oedema, and the patient died 5 days after treatment, with marked rises in interferon-gamma, GM-CSF, tumour necrosis factor-alpha, interleukin-6 and interleukin-10. At autopsy multiple organs showed systemic ischaemia and haemorrhagic microangiopathic injury and the lungs diffuse alveolar damage; histological examination of autopsy tissue found ERBB2 at 3+ in liver metastases and 2+ in lung metastases and much lower levels in normal lung parenchyma, normal liver and normal breast. The authors hypothesised that highly active ERBB2-directed T cells recognised ERBB2 on normal lung cells on first pass through the lung and released inflammatory cytokines that began a cascade ending in multiorgan failure; the autopsy findings were read as initial lung injury followed by days of hypotension and ischaemia, and the authors call the significance of the cells' reactivity against cultured primary cells unclear. This is a single case, with a stated dose and conditioning, whose mechanism is the authors' hypothesis and which gives no incidence for any CAR product (Morgan et al., 2010). In a trial of an affinity-enhanced T-cell receptor against HLA-A*01-restricted MAGE-A3 in myeloma and melanoma, the first two patients developed cardiogenic shock and died within days; no MAGE-A3 expression was detected in heart tissue at autopsy, and beating cardiomyocytes made from induced pluripotent stem cells triggered T-cell killing through recognition of an unrelated peptide from titin. That is off-target recognition of an unintended molecule, not the intended target in the wrong tissue (Linette et al., 2013).

How the question is asked before and during trials. FDA's CAR T-cell development guidance says to assess both undesired targeting of healthy tissue that expresses the intended antigen (on-target/off-tumour) and unintended targeting of other antigens, using examples such as tissue cross-reactivity studies with an antibody carrying the same recognition domain, protein arrays, cytotoxicity and cytokine-release testing on panels of primary cells, cell lines or stem-cell-derived organ systems, and relevant animal models, and encourages a combination of methods; antigen recognition domains can differ in affinity or avidity or recognise a different site, which should be evaluated, and CAR T cells can carry added components such as suicide genes. No universal expression cut-off is given here because no source read gives one. Whether affinity tuning, recognition logic or control switches improve safety for a particular design needs that design's own evidence. The 2026 ASTCT consensus abstract lists on-target, off-tumour toxicity among the toxicities for which it considered definitions and grading; its criteria were not readable.

rows.sourceScope: Denkert 2021 resolved raw abstract; no universal TNBC prevalence inferred.

rows.section: The real candidates in triple-negative breast cancer
rows.requirement: Keep HER2-low staining separate from indication eligibility and product-specific cardiac assessment; verify the cited LVEF monitoring requirement without an individual monitoring instruction.
rows.disposition: represented in registered audit-draft fields at stated source scope

evidence.excerpt: Expression and clinical eligibility are different from organ-risk assessment. The U.S. ENHERTU label calls for assessment of left-ventricular ejection fraction before treatment and at regular intervals during treatment as clinically indicated. It does not turn a HER2 score into a personal monitoring schedule or establish that a tumour-expression category predicts cardiac injury.

Approved in HER2+ metastatic breast cancer (DESTINY-Breast03: beat T-DM1), HER2-low (DESTINY-Breast04, 2022) and HER2-ultralow (DESTINY-Breast06, 2025) HR+ breast cancer, HER2+ gastric, HER2-mutant NSCLC, and tumour-agnostically for HER2 IHC 3+ solid tumours (2024). DESTINY-Breast09 (with pertuzumab) established it in first-line HER2+ metastatic disease. In Q2 2026 the FDA approved two early-stage HER2+ indications (neoadjuvant DESTINY-Breast11; post-neoadjuvant DESTINY-Breast05). Interstitial lung disease (~10-15%, ~1% fatal) requires monitoring. Membrane-permeable payload gives a strong bystander effect.

rows.entailment: HER2 score, indication and cardiac assessment are distinct; before-treatment and regular clinically indicated LVEF assessment is label-scoped.
rows.sourceScope: ENHERTU section 5.3 read directly, not a personal monitoring instruction.

rows.section: The real candidates in triple-negative breast cancer
rows.requirement: Nectin-4 normal-tissue findings do not establish a safety advantage; retain the enfortumab severe/fatal skin warning and resolve any cited alternative normal-expression surveys before use.
rows.disposition: represented in registered audit-draft fields at stated source scope

evidence.excerpt: M-Rabet's 2017 study found membranous Nectin-4 staining in 62% of 61 TNBCs and did not detect protein in the adult normal tissues examined by that assay. That negative assay result is not universal normal-tissue absence or a safety advantage. PADCEV, a different finished Nectin-4-directed construct, carries a boxed warning for severe and fatal skin reactions. Keep antibody, preparation, tissue coverage, detection limits, product and exposure with the comparison.

The PADCEV label reports EV-302: enfortumab vedotin plus intravenous pembrolizumab versus cisplatin or carboplatin with gemcitabine in previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer. Median overall survival was 31.5 versus 16.1 months, hazard ratio 0.47. Those results belong to this combination, population and comparator.

A Nectin-4 stain alone does not establish the finished product's safety or benefit in another cancer. The label carries a boxed warning for severe and fatal skin reactions; other indications, eligibility conditions and safety requirements remain product-specific.

rows.entailment: A negative normal-tissue assay does not establish a safety advantage; severe/fatal skin reactions remain an actual product warning.
rows.sourceScope: M-Rabet assay-specific abstract and PADCEV boxed warning. No unread alternative normal-tissue survey is adopted.

rows.section: The real candidates in triple-negative breast cancer
rows.requirement: Resolve EV-202 and verify 42 advanced-TNBC participants, confirmed ORR 19.0% and disease control 57.1%, with study threshold and noncomparative design rather than a target ranking.
rows.disposition: represented in registered audit-draft fields at stated source scope

evidence.excerpt: Giordano's 2025 publication reports enfortumab-vedotin monotherapy in 45 women with hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer and 42 with TNBC after prior treatment. In the TNBC cohort, confirmed objective response was 19.0% and disease control 57.1%. Activity did not meet the prespecified threshold, and the study reported no trend between Nectin-4 expression and response. This is a nonrandomised phase 2 cohort, not a comparison with a TROP2 ADC or a demonstration of target superiority.

EV-202 (NCT04225117) is an open-label, nonrandomised, multicohort phase 2 study of enfortumab vedotin, with additional combination cohorts. The ClinicalTrials.gov entry checked on 11 November 2026 lists 329 participants overall, active but not recruiting status, and actual primary completion on 25 February 2025. Its overall programme and intervention list should not be confused with one published disease cohort.

rows.entailment: 42 TNBC participants, ORR 19.0%, DCR 57.1%, failure to meet the threshold and nonrandomised design remain separate from the whole 329-person programme.
rows.sourceScope: Raw Crossref publisher-registered abstract and current registry; no numeric threshold is invented from blocked publisher text.

rows.section: The real candidates in triple-negative breast cancer
rows.requirement: Keep B7-H3 dual-compartment preclinical work separate from a verified TNBC prevalence estimate or breast approval.
rows.disposition: represented in registered audit-draft fields at stated source scope

evidence.excerpt: B7-H3, also called CD276, has been studied on cancer cells and tumour-associated vessels. Expression in a tissue sample is different from accessible binding, delivered active material and clinical benefit. Preclinical compartment-targeting experiments and clinical trial registrations answer different questions; neither supplies a universal expression threshold or a breast-cancer prevalence estimate.

Seaman's 2017 preclinical work compared defined CD276 conjugates in mouse tumour models. The MMAE construct acted on CD276-positive cancer cells but did not effectively ablate tumour vessels; the PBD construct acted on both compartments and eradicated large established tumours and metastases in the reported models. Preserve the particular antibody, payload, compartment and model. This result does not mean that every B7-H3 payload will behave alike or establish the frequency of expression or benefit in people with breast cancer.

rows.entailment: Preclinical compartments do not supply a validated TNBC prevalence or a breast indication.
rows.sourceScope: Premise-backed interpretation of separately measured quantities; not a new empirical or clinical result.

rows.section: The real candidates in triple-negative breast cancer
rows.requirement: Verify the three named ifinatamab phase-3 registry states and their lung, prostate and oesophageal populations at a dated capture; registry phase/recruitment is not efficacy or access.
rows.disposition: represented in registered audit-draft fields at stated source scope

evidence.excerpt: In the ClinicalTrials.gov entries checked on 11 November 2026, three named ifinatamab deruxtecan studies were phase 3 and recruiting: NCT06203210 in relapsed small-cell lung cancer, NCT06925737 in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and NCT06644781 in previously treated advanced or metastatic oesophageal squamous-cell cancer. Their diseases and comparators remain separate. Phase and recruitment are dated registry facts, not reported efficacy, an approval decision, guaranteed enrolment or a breast-cancer indication.

IDeate-Lung02 (NCT06203210) compares ifinatamab deruxtecan with physician-choice topotecan, amrubicin or lurbinectedin in relapsed small-cell lung cancer. The ClinicalTrials.gov entry checked on 11 November 2026 lists overall survival as the primary outcome; objective response is a secondary outcome. The study is phase 3 and recruiting, with no results posted in that entry. It does not compare directly with tarlatamab or establish a treatment sequence.

rows.entailment: Each of three dated phase 3 recruiting studies keeps its actual disease. The Lung02 primary outcome is OS, with response secondary, and no posted results.
rows.sourceScope: Six raw registry records selected identity/status/condition/phase/outcome fields; no protocol-wide or access claim.

rows.section: The real candidates in triple-negative breast cancer
rows.requirement: Resolve Sussman LIV-1 expression, hormonal-treatment retention, TNBC upregulation and specific conjugate trafficking; cancer-type expression does not supply a normal-tissue denominator.
rows.disposition: represented in registered audit-draft fields at stated source scope

evidence.excerpt:
LIV-1 (SLC39A6) is a zinc transporter investigated as a delivery target. Sussman's 2014 work reported expression retained after hormonal therapy in primary and metastatic breast specimens, upregulation in triple-negative breast cancer, and expression in several other cancer types. These observations do not provide one universal TNBC prevalence or a normal-tissue denominator.

The specified SGN-LIV1A construct used an MMAE payload. In tested cell lines it was internalised and trafficked to lysosomes, with activity in cell and tumour models. That supports preclinical development, not a validated clinical target or a response guarantee for every LIV-1-positive tumour.

rows.entailment: Sussman's expression, hormonal-treatment retention, TNBC upregulation and actual MMAE trafficking model are separate from a normal-tissue denominator or clinical validation.
rows.sourceScope: Sussman 2014 resolved raw abstract.

rows.section: The real candidates in triple-negative breast cancer
rows.requirement: Verify the two ladiratuzumab registry completion states independently of approval or current availability; a completed trial is not an approved therapy.
rows.disposition: represented in registered audit-draft fields at stated source scope

evidence.excerpt: The ClinicalTrials.gov entries checked on 11 November 2026 list NCT01969643, the ladiratuzumab-vedotin study, as completed and NCT03310957, its pembrolizumab combination study, as completed. These are study states, not evidence of regulatory approval, an open treatment site or present drug availability. A statement about expression in other cancer types also does not establish how much accessible LIV-1 is present in normal tissues.

rows.entailment: Both ladiratuzumab study states are completed, not terminated; completion does not establish approval, an open site or availability.
rows.sourceScope: Two raw ClinicalTrials.gov status records checked on 11 November 2026.

rows.section: The real candidates in triple-negative breast cancer
rows.requirement: Assess the TROP2-wins/Nectin-4-better-but-lost ranking: different assays, cohorts, products and study designs do not establish a direct comparative target, safety or clinical-efficacy hierarchy.

evidence.excerpt: A staining prevalence, activity of an experimental conjugate in a mouse and a response rate in a nonrandomised clinical cohort are different observations. The EV-202 breast-cohort results are on the trial record. Comparing them with a different product's randomised trial or an unrelated tissue survey cannot rank Nectin-4 against TROP2 as an intrinsically better target, a safer target or a more effective clinical choice.

Two retrospective TNBC series used different assays. Jacot's 2025 nonmetastatic series used the Enzo ENZ-ABS380 antibody and H-scores below 100, 100 to 200, and above 200: 225 of 228 tumours had membrane expression and 58.8% were in the strong group. Izci's 2022 series included 685 patients overall, with 589 scored for these groups using Abcam ab227689: 97 high (201 to 300), 149 medium (100 to 200) and 343 low (below 100), or 16.5%, 25.3% and 58.2%. These are assay- and cohort-specific distributions, not harmonised prevalence estimates or validated individual treatment thresholds.

rows.entailment: Unrelated tissue surveys, a phase 2 cohort and randomised trials cannot rank the intrinsic target, safety or product efficacy.
rows.sourceScope: Premise-backed interpretation of separately measured quantities; not a new empirical or clinical result.

rows.requirement: For a fictional 85%-positive/minimal-normal-staining proposal, require antibody/cutoff/cohort, cells per tumour, normal tissues/method, full-product distribution, processing and payload evidence; no IHC rate alone validates the address.

evidence.excerpt: Stepan's 2011 transcript and protein survey found substantial TROP2 expression in several essential normal tissues. Tumour enrichment and a current label's lack of a TROP2 selection test answer different questions from accessible normal-tissue expression and the finished product's therapeutic window. A fictional 85%-positive, minimally normal-staining proposal still needs the antibody, cutoff, cohort, positive-cell distribution within tumours, normal tissues and methods, and full-product distribution, processing and response evidence. A single stain or an antigen count does not supply those results.

Choosing a surface address involves its measured amount, accessible normal-tissue distribution, behaviour with the actual format and variation within and between lesions. One positive core at one date cannot survey the whole tumour. A static receptor count and a manufactured loading ratio do not alone determine cumulative delivery across receptor turnover, repeated encounters and release over time. ADC uptake and processing are construct-specific; antibody retention can matter to radiation delivery, and engager contact geometry and useful effectors matter to immune recruitment. No universal antigen-density cutoff or low-density format ranking follows from a platform name. Damelin's 2015 survey found a broad range of normal- and tumour-tissue expression among the ADC targets studied and could not formalise optimal target parameters within that set. It does not show that useful target selection is impossible.

rows.entailment: The fictional 85% claim still needs assay/cutoff/cohort, within-tumour and normal-tissue coverage, and full-product delivery and response evidence.
rows.sourceScope: Premise-backed interpretation of separately measured quantities; not a new empirical or clinical result.
